summary: TLS SNI selection results in mixed egress edges, causing intermittent cross-region p95 latency increases for EU tenant
description:
Issue summary: NimbusAI reported intermittent increases in end-to-end p95 latency for requests from EU clients beginning 2026-03-09. Root cause suspicion: client requests occasionally route to a US-edge due to TLS SNI selection at the edge proxy, resulting in cross-region egress and added TLS handshake time.

Impact: Customer-facing inference experiences 200-800ms p95 spikes for streaming and non-streaming calls; affects SLA-bound workflows for enterprise customer (billing + availability concerns). Not a total outage—requests succeed but latency is elevated and inconsistent.

Environment: prod | eu-west; tenant scoped (NimbusAI account). Observed across multiple model routes (rw-instruction-7b, open-instruct-3b).

Observed behavior: Traffic from EU clients intermittently terminates at an edge node whose TLS SNI selection maps to us-east egress path. Datadog traces show additional 1–2 TLS handshakes and an extra network hop.

Expected behavior: Control-plane residency pin and edge selection should produce stable eu-west egress for pinned tenants with deterministic SNI mapping.

Initial customer-reported symptoms: "We see sudden latency spikes near p95 on the last two days—most calls are fine but every few minutes a request takes an extra 600ms and traces show a US hop."
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use tenant API key for NimbusAI (prod) from a eu-west client IP range
2) Send sustained streaming requests at ~5 QPS over 10 minutes to rw-instruction-7b endpoint
3) Observe p95 latency in client telemetry and collect X-Edge-Trace headers when spike occurs
4) Correlate with Datadog trace IDs and edge-proxy access logs (referenced below)
logs: Datadog trace example: https://app.datadoghq.com/trace/trace_id=5f3a... (redacted) - shows extra TLS handshake and 120ms+ RTT to us-east edge
Edge proxy access logs: sni=tenant-nimbus.example.com selected_edge=us-east-1a x_forwarded_for=... timestamp=2026-03-09T14:22:31Z
Residency service timeline: control-plane pin refresh for tenant occurred at 2026-03-09T14:21:58Z (possible race window)
Auth token binding logs: token-scoped residency header present in 94% of requests, missing in 6% correlating with spikes
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:40 - Support initial triage: confirmed customer p95 spikes correlate with occasional egress to us-east edges.
Hypothesis A: edge-proxy SNI selection falling back to generic SNI mapping when token-scoped residency header absent or trimmed by client (browser preconnect behavior).
Hypothesis B: control-plane residency metadata propagation lag during pin refresh (control-plane reported a 4s propagation delay to some edge caches).
Repro attempt: Forced removal of token-scoped residency header from test requests reproduced egress hop in local lab, indicating header presence is a strong factor.
Trace/metric artifacts: p95 latency increases align with a spike in TLS handshake duration and DNS re-resolve events on edge (see dd metric: edge.tls.handshake.duration.p95).
Cross-check with SUP-210999: similar egress detours reported during control-plane syncs; may be related to same propagation window.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:05 - Aisha Kumar (Support): 'Thanks NimbusAI team — we've reproduced a deterministic case where missing token residency header results in SNI-based fallback to default edge. We're escalating to Edge SRE. Attaching traces.'

2026-03-10 11:12 - Liam O'Connor (Edge SRE): 'I see two likely vectors: (1) client preconnect / browser DNS preresolve causing an initial SNI to be picked up by a global LB before residency header is processed, (2) small control-plane cache TTL mismatch. I'll instrument edge to log SNI->tenant mapping decisions.'

2026-03-10 15:48 - NimbusAI Support Rep (Customer): 'We confirmed that adding a short header override on our side (X-Residence: eu-west) removed spikes during the afternoon test window. We need a long-term fix.'
2026-03-11 09:30 - Liam O'Connor (Edge SRE): 'Workaround applied: edge proxy config updated to prefer token-scoped residency when present in early TLS passthrough path. Monitoring for 24h.'
2026-03-12 08:04 - Aisha Kumar (Support): 'Customer confirmatory test in EU shows >90% reduction in p95 spikes since workaround. Closing in on a permanent change in control plane.'
resolution: Applied short-term workaround (edge proxy preference change to favor token-scoped residency earlier in request lifecycle). Customer reports ~90% reduction in p95 spikes. Next steps: (1) Engineering to add invariant SNI mapping behavior when residency pin exists (PR in progress: https://github.com/redwood-infra/edge-proxy/pull/1197), (2) Reduce control-plane propagation TTLs and add a reconciliation job to avoid temporary cache misses, (3) Add telemetry to detect missing residency headers and auto-alert. ETA for permanent fix: 2026-03-20. Follow-up: schedule postmortem and update residency runbook.
